But I agree, this simplifies things.

issue_context.title: Add spring.webflux.multipart configuration properties
issue_context.body:
See spring-projects/spring-framework#26790 for background information.

We could provide configuration properties to make the multipart configuration easier with WebFlux. Currently this is supported by `org.springframework.http.codec.multipart.DefaultPartHttpMessageReader`. Note that we need to carefully consider the configuration keys, as several of them don't apply if the "streaming" mode is selected.

review_comments: There may be a more tactical class(es) to use for this - I used what the auto-config is directly operating on.
I see it in your merge commit (`WebConfigurer.class`)
I chose to pull these defaults out to well-named vars to make the tests clear when the reader was using a default vs. when it had its value changed by the customizer.
Order is 1 so that it runs after the more generic CodecCustomizer which is at order 0. What is the recommended way to document these ordering relationships?

My DRY alarm is going off... however, I think the repetition is just at the cusp of acceptable. I made a pass at factoring out some of the common things between the tests but their slight differences are just enough that it was not an improvement (it was less readable).
